items.excerpt: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year;
items.body: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year; it signalled the arrival of George Clinton’s ensemble as the next great voice in Black rock and psychedelia. In his 2014 memoir Brothas Be, Yo Like George, Ain’t That Funkin’ Kinda Hard On You?, Clinton acknowledges this by contrasting the album’s release with Hendrix’s death, an event that he notes as “the end of an era”. During his brief but electrifying career, Hendrix moulded multiple aspects of the Black musical tradition – blues, rock, funk, R&B, jazz – into an electrifying corpus that opened up a new world of possibilities. With Hendrix dead and the psychedelic road map that he laid out for any adventurous soul to follow, Funkadelic went on to emerge as his mightiest descendents. While Funkadelic were recording Free Your Mind Clinton absorbed and pulled inspiration from underground comics, Black power/radical leftist theory and Erich von Däniken’s work theorising that aliens had made contact with and shaped the development of ancient human civilisations. Clinton took all the disparate cultural, historical, political and extraterrestrial influences swirling around in his head and drenched them in acid. The famously LSD soaked sessions produced an album that distilled the political, cultural and philosophical DNA of the 1960s into a new musical vision for the 70s. Built around Eddie Hazel’s gnarly blues and wah-wah drenched guitar, “Funky Dollar Bill” highlights the flipside of the concept of money as freedom explored on “Friday Night, August 14th”. With lyrics like "The pusher push, the fixer fix, the judge acquits, the junkie leads his life, for the dollar bill”, it's clear that here, money is less a vehicle for freedom than a tool for control. “Eulogy And Light” serves as the perfect album closer, with Clinton praying for strength in the face of temptation and moral degradation. In an innovative display of the band's willingness to experiment with sound and concepts, the music for “Eulogy And Light” is an earlier Funkadelic track called “Open Your Eyes” spun backwards. In doing this, Clinton and crew extract the source song's optimistic heart and repurpose its gospel-inspired tune into something stranger, more twisted. Free Your Mind opens with the epic ten minute title track. Amid a ghostly mass of distorted guitar, feedback and cosmic synthesizer bleeps, Clinton screams “Free your mind and your ass will follow/The kingdom of heaven is within!”. These simple yet spine-tingling chants formed something close to a succinct mission statement. More than just slogans, Clinton was directly addressing the intellectual, physical and spiritual demands of a new musical and ideological path. He has described “Friday Night, August 14th” as a “paycheck and party song” about how a little bit of money can buy a moment of joy and freedom. In that sense, the song feels like the spiritual heir to Louis Jordan's 1949 proto-rock ’n’ roll smash “Saturday Night Fish Fry”. By the time Funkadelic entered the United Sound Systems studio in Detroit to record the follow-up to Free Your Mind, the band were at once a formidable live unit and boundless experimenters in the studio. The result of those USS sessions was 1971’s Maggot Brain, one of the greatest psychedelic rock albums ever made and the crown jewel of Clinton’s extensive body of work. The album opens with a simple and ominous message that is both a continuation of the core theme examined throughout Free Your Mind and a harbinger of the band’s future: “I have tasted the maggots in the mind of the universe/I was not offended/For I knew I had to rise above it all/Or drown in my own shit”. Here the “maggots” are the corrosive forces of ignorance, self-doubt and control that infested Free Your Mind. To all intents and purposes, Maggot Brain is a trip through the other side of enlightenment, witnessed through the prism of life, death and the liberatory potential of madness. Famously, Clinton prompted guitarist Eddie Hazel to imagine that his mother had died before recording Maggot Brain’s almost ten minute long title track. Hazel transforms his guitar into a wailing and mourning instrument of grief. Beneath his solo, a dreamy, six note arpeggio acts as the bedrock to one of the greatest guitar performances ever captured on tape. “Can You Get To That” flips the energy from dark to light with its slick groove and doo-wop harmonies. A bright and joyous song at face value, the lyrics warn that even in death, no one escapes karma. “Hit It And Quit It” is a flamboyant acid rock tune with an odd metre that betrays Funkadelic's debt to both the church and the temple of Jimi Hendrix. For an outfit that proved so adept at conjuring colourful, funky images of utopia, it's curious that they chose to close out their greatest album with “Wars Of Armageddon”. Clocking in at over nine minutes long, the song is a minefield of explosions, screams and fuzzed-out guitars. The chants of “More power to the people/More pussy to the power” offer a reminder that Funkadelic’s psychedelic ideals and ambitions never strayed too far from the funky, carnal physicality of life on Earth. This review appears in The Wire 512 along with many other reviews of new and recent records, books, films, festivals and more. To read them all, pick up a copy of the magazine in our online shop. Wire subscribers can also read the issue in our online magazine library.

Soft Machine were pioneers really, being one of the most influential psychedelic/progressive acts of their time. This album, their debut, the only with Kevin Ayers on, is so exciting because of the top notch musicianship despite being difficult to follow on some parts. Really amazing blend of jazz/rock/pop that keeps you interested along the way.Really groovy rhythm section with Kevin Ayers on bass and Robert Wyatt on drums who is also doing the vocals. Mike Ratledge on organ on the other hand, like his British peers on that time, is truly mesmerizing.

items.body: Halcyon eyes, kind of gloomy in-between (If not now, then when we gonna do it, baby?) Holy pledge, Nostradamus said we’re clean (If not you, then who is gonna teach it to me?) PONS have somehow made a song that sounds as though a demon discovered stimulants, bought an expensive string section, read half a book about Roman emperors, and immediately decided he ought to run for king of hell. IF NOT NOW… is five-plus minutes of Brooklyn dance-punk delirium built around repetition as both engine and psychological hazard. Jack Parker and company plant a krautrock riff in the floorboards, then proceed to furnish the room with strings, horns, electronic abrasion, post-punk angles, and enough manic forward motion to make stopping seem medically inadvisable. Somewhere between Suicide, Brainiac, Liars, Sextile, and Ecce Schnak, after several catastrophic decisions, PONS turn excess into an organizing principle. Parker admits that excess comes naturally. “I have a really maximalist impulse when I’m writing music that I’ve recently been trying to get away from.” You can hear him losing that argument in spectacular fashion. The Eclectica String Quartet enters the picture alongside arrangements refined with Steve La Rosa, and suddenly the song has the air of an espionage film whose secret agent has misplaced the microfilm and joined a Dionysian cult instead. The repetition is crucial. PONS keep worrying the central figure until familiarity starts producing strange side effects, with each return carrying another detail, another escalation, another reason to suspect somebody has slipped something questionable into the punch. Parker wanted “something as repetitive and hypnotic as possible,” and the band stretches that idea toward absurdity without losing its grip on the dance floor. Lyrically, appetite keeps mutating. Sex, ambition, prophecy, intoxication, history, conquest, divine entitlement, and cultural memory pile together until the speaker begins sounding less like a romantic opportunist than somebody preparing to annex a small republic before breakfast. Desire becomes destiny; destiny develops an ego problem. By the closing stretch, bravery, brutality, providence, and personal mythology have become indistinguishable enough to suggest that civilization may have been a clerical error. Animator Arturo Baston pushes the same madness into the accompanying video. “Arturo had the idea of animating some sort of nightmare carnival bumper car ride filled with freaks and ghouls,” says Parker. From there, Parker becomes a Ghost Rider-like figure traveling through the underworld on his way toward infernal royalty, because apparently ordinary professional advancement was unavailable. Watch the video for If NOT NOW… below: IF NOT NOW… belongs to the forthcoming RACECAR, out November 5 via Casa Gogol Records, Eugene Hütz’s new label. If this single represents the album’s governing philosophy, PONS have built themselves a machine whose accelerator has been welded permanently to the floor. Normies should probably stand clear. Listen to IF NOT NOW… below and order the single here. You can pre-order RACECAR here. items._cn_summary: PONS 来自布鲁克林，这首作品以重复性极强的迷幻律动为骨架，融合了弦乐四重奏、铜管、电子噪音与后朋克棱角，形成一种接近失控的嘉年华式密集编排。乐队坦言自身具有极端的'最大化'冲动——在创作中刻意堆叠元素，将过度本身变成组织原则。弦乐部分由 Ecce Schnak 弦乐四重奏担纲，与制作人 Steve La Rosa 共同打磨，赋予作品间谍电影式的荒诞气质。歌词层面，欲望、野心、预言、征服欲不断叠加膨胀，直至说话者从浪漫投机者蜕变为准备吞并小国的僭主。视觉上，动画师 Arturo Baston 打造了一座充满怪物与恶鬼的噩梦旋转木马，主角穿越冥界向地狱王权进发。该曲收录于即将由 Casa Gogol Records 发行的专辑 RACECAR，是一支在后朋克躯壳下进行实验性跨界探索的独立乐队作品。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Lucro Sucio; Los Ojos del Vacio' is the unexpected, overly mysterious, and definitely dream-likeninth studio album by The Mars Volta, released in April of 2025 through Clouds Hill, serving as thefollow-up to 2022's self-titled LP and its acoustic follow-up from the following year. The reformedband features an interesting lineup that sees masterminds Omar Rodriguez Lopez and Cedric Bixler-Zavala joined by Omar's brother Marcel, who plays some keyboards and is involved in the engineeringof the album, versatile female drummer Philo Tsoungui, keyboardist-saxophonist Leo Genovese, andbass player Josh Moreau, a session player with some serious experiences in well-known rock andalternative bands. As for the album in question, 'Lucro Sucio' is an 18-track labyrinth of hazy andethereal synth soundscapes, indulgent jazzy interludes, and meditative psychedelic melodies,elevated by the iconic voice of Bixler-Zavala, who sounds as solid as ever on this LP.What I really like about this record is how the gently protruding latin rock elements from the twoprevious albums have been preserved on 'Lucro Sucio', but with an artsy, cryptic undercurrent. Thereis also a very generous interpolation of various synths that allows the pristine production to shinethrough, while the tranquil, ambient tones that prevail give the collection a somewhat ominous, hazyfeel. Leaning more towards trippy art rock than prog, 'Lucro Sucio' is not necessarily the mostsubstantial Mars Volta album, especially when compared to some of the band's intimidating andmaximalist early classics. It almost feels as if Omar and Cedric are attempting to capture theopposite of what their early releases had represented, and to be honest, there is something daringand novel in such a risky experiment. The album is innovative yet accessible, with an abundance ofbeautifully composed electronic-laden psychedelic pieces like 'Reina Tormenta/Enlazan lasTinieblas', 'Cue the Sun/Alba del Orate', 'Poseedora de Mi Sombra', 'Vocifer�', and 'Un Disparo alVac�o'.The finale is a little too monotonous for my taste (that would be last five tracks), but the factthat the entire work weaves through like one continuous piece makes it more diverse and immersivethan the band's 2022 self-titled release. Nevertheless, 'Lucro Sucio' is tame and ethereal, whichfor longtime listeners of the band represents just one side of The Mars Volta's expansive studiosound.

items._cn_summary: The Mars Volta 第九张录音室专辑由 Omar Rodriguez-Lopez 与 Cedric Bixler-Zavala 主导，集合多位乐手共同打造。整张专辑以十八首曲目串联成连续流动的整体，核心特征是朦胧空灵的合成器音景、爵士即兴段落与冥想式迷幻旋律的交织。拉丁摇滚元素得以延续，但被包裹在艺术化与隐秘化的氛围之中。Bixler-Zavala 的人声贯穿始终，依然是稳定的核心。制作精良，电子化的迷幻篇章占据了专辑最出色的部分，如《Reina Tormenta》《Cue the Sun》等曲目。评论者指出末段五首稍显单调，且与乐队早期繁复宏大的风格相比，整体走向了克制与空灵的一端。这是一张偏向氛围化与实验性平衡的专辑，对于偏好前卫与电子融合的听众具有吸引力。

items.body:
There is a substantial list of attributes that sets Ran Blake apart from every other innovative pianist of the past sixty-plus years, each of which falls under one of two headings: his choice of materials and his treatments of them. The former is based on Blake’s ability to hear connections between materials for which “disparate” is an inadequate descriptor. Who else would sequence Max Roach’s “Mendacity” and “Saving All My Love for You” – or “On Top of Old Smokey” and Michel Legrand’s “Watch What Happens”? Nobody, because what Blake does is unique. He doesn’t interpret materials as much as administer an MRI, revealing the connective tissues and vital organs as vividly, if not more so, than the skeletal structure. In the process, Blake makes the familiar sound radically new.

Blake’s collaborations with singers are central to his work. The current critical consensus is that his groundbreaking work with Jeanne Lee overshadows everything since, the respective qualities of notables like Christine Correa and Sara Serpa notwithstanding. Roots & Byways circumvents the edifice The Newest Sound Around has become, primarily because Dominique Eade takes a different tact. She is not as rooted as Correa – or Lee, for that matter – in Billie Holiday, and she is not as committed to understatement as Serpa. Like both Correa and Serpa, Eade can shape a song syllable by syllable and render a highly personal interpretation. It is Eade’s palpably deep joy in singing that sets her apart, one that is not only bursting at the seams on showstoppers like the Whitney Houston megahit, but one that even seeps into noirish songs like Mingus’ “Portrait.” It is the key to her relatability and appeal, and to that of the album, as well.

items._cn_summary: Ran Blake与歌手Dominique Eade合作的专辑展示了Blake标志性的解构式钢琴美学：他不演奏既有曲目，而是通过类MRI式的扫描，将看似毫无关联的素材并置——从Max Roach的硬波普到Whitney Houston的流行金曲，从民谣到Michel Legrand的电影配乐，暴露出作品内部被忽视的肌理与骨架。这种曲目编排逻辑极度个人化，在当代爵士界几乎无人效仿。Eade的声乐处理避开了Billie Holiday式的深沉根脉与Sara Serpa式的克制低调，转而强调歌唱中迸发的深层喜悦，使暗色调的Mingus作品与流行大热曲目在同一空间内共处。专辑通过对唱词逐音节的精密塑形与高度个人化的诠释，在实验性与可听性之间找到平衡，既保留了先锋爵士的智性挑战，也具备触动普通听众的情感通道。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items.album: Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari
items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items.label: Songs of Compassion
items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 携手作曲家 Paladino 与诗人 Ferrari 推出《Songs of Compassion》，以钢琴为核心、辅以弦乐、木管与合成器铺陈，构建非线性的聆听结构。乐评将其归入史蒂夫·赖希与菲利普·格拉斯一脉的简约与序列语汇，而非传统和声进行，旋律如意识流般随歌词起伏。Mokowitz 的演唱带有阅历感，人声与钢琴互为补充，音乐则以脉冲与不协和框定氛围。歌词延续1960年代抗议传统，直面威权主义、新纳粹与种族议题，同时穿插对死亡与宇宙位置的沉思。整张专辑将政治表达、诗歌性与实验声响融合，呈现一种觉醒年代式的思辨美学。

The Gods Laugh
certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody o
items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 这支乐队的核心特色在于完全使用自制的非常规乐器进行演奏，包括tassofons、tilofons、clarinuts、didjerimou和klarbass等以废弃物和边角料打造的装置，且在现代录音条件下依然保持音准和音色品质。专辑将多种文化音乐风格融入创作：klezmer旋律、cumbia节奏、afrobeat打击乐质感、samba律动以及中东音阶交替出现，乐手在这些风格框架中进行即兴演奏，展现出跨文化融合的演奏功底。专辑传达的核心信息是音乐的普世性——无论乐器材质如何，音乐家总能找到发声的方式，这一概念通过他们自制的"厨房乐器"得到具体体现。整体融合实验手工乐器与世界音乐传统，是一张充满趣味和原创性的跨界作品。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这是挪威Camilla Hole Trio在探索星际合成器声响后的回归之作，回归本土挪威民俗音乐素材。乐队以高音萨克斯为主奏，与低音提琴和鼓构成三重奏框架，融入模块合成器与颤音琴的音色层次。他们对传统挪威西部春舞配乐进行重新诠释，开篇由萨克斯陈述旋律，鼓与贝斯提供节奏支撑，合成器与颤音琴以叠加方式增添色彩。乐队成员角色不断流动，贝斯手接替旋律与萨克斯齐奏，鼓手进一步拓展节奏空间，整体走向自由的即兴表达，最后萨克斯在结尾处再次回归主题。作品模糊了爵士即兴与挪威民间舞曲的边界。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威乐手组成三重奏，以非传统方式演绎斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材。乐评将其比作室内乐而非舞蹈伴奏音乐，强调三位演奏者在音乐亲密对话中的沉浸感。Tellef Kvifte 主要使用竖笛（recorder），结合萨克斯与风笛等北欧传统之外的乐器，其子 Knut Kvifte Nesheim 担任鼓手与作曲，三人致力于模糊不同音乐类型的界限。专辑以挪威 Setesdal 山谷的著名小提琴曲《Fossgrimen》开篇，呼应民间传说中瀑布精灵传授琴技的神秘意象，揭示北欧舞曲表面欢愉之下的暗流。瑞典 polska 曲目的演绎中，旋律在引入后迅速碎片化并戛然而止，展现出对传统素材隐藏可能性的探索。整体呈现出实验性室内即兴与传统民间音乐的深度融合。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — Miles Davis released three albums in 1968. Nefertiti, Miles in the sky and Filles de Kilimanjaro. FdK is the least rated on this website but is my favorite out of these three records. Like any other Miles Davis album of course, this one as well is consisting of an all-star line up of musicians and that alone is a good enough reason to listen to as many as possible Davis records you can. The musicianship is always fantastic. The album kicks of really strong, and then becomes mellower yet really beautiful. The perfect epilogue before the Miles Davis electric and frantic period of jazz/rock records.
items._cn_summary: 这是Miles Davis 1968年三张专辑中最不被ProgArchives重视的一张，却被作者视为个人最爱。专辑延续了Davis一贯的全明星阵容传统，演奏水平精湛。开场部分强劲有力，随后转入柔和优美的段落，形成鲜明对比。作为Davis进入电气化、狂热爵士/摇滚时期之前的完美终章，这张作品处于其风格转折的过渡阶段——既保留了传统爵士的精致与即兴空间，又开始吸收放克与摇滚节奏元素，为后续的Bitches Brew等实验性作品铺设了路径。整体展现了Davis在爵士融合转型期的探索意图。

items.body: La Feria returns to Liverpool this October for its eighth edition, spreading five days of Latin American music, theatre, dance, visual art and food from Hope Street down to Chinatown. The festival was launched in 2018 by Luma Creations, the Liverpool organisation led by Chilean-born songwriter Francisco Carrasco, to put artists from across Latin America and its British diaspora on the city’s stages. This year’s music starts in Chile, with songs built on the Andean rhythms of huayno and tinku and with folk tunes opened up through jazz improvisation. From there it moves to the brass-heavy mambo and salsa dura of a 13-piece Latin big band, to Afro-Colombian gaita flute set over electronic beats and deep bass, and to Brazilian forró and coco rhythms reworked as pop. Around the evening concerts and theatre performances, the week also brings a visual art exhibition, free workshops led by visiting artists, and two free family days to close the festival at the weekend. On Wednesday, Unity Theatre opens the festival with Manuelita, a one-woman show from Popelei in which Tamsin Hurtado Clarke takes on Manuela Sáenz. The Quito-born revolutionary fought through the independence wars at Simón Bolívar’s side, and in 1828 she helped him escape an attempt on his life in Bogotá. Hurtado Clarke tells her story through comedy and physical theatre to music by Colombian guitarist Camilo Menjura. Before the play, 18-year-old Argentine-British musician Eli Rowley plays Argentine and Andean tunes on the ronroco, a big-bodied, low-tuned relative of the charango, taking his cues from Gustavo Santaolalla and Jaime Torres. A short walk from Unity Theatre, the Music Room at Liverpool Philharmonic Hall takes over on Thursday, when Camila y Silvio return after selling out at La Feria in 2022. Camila Soria and Silvio Rozzi met during Chile’s student protests in 2011, and in 2015 they toured Argentina at length, learning the traditional styles of that country and the Andes. Their music moves between huayno, tinku, chacarera and vidala, with two voices over Rozzi’s guitar and charango and the deep thump of Soria’s bombo legüero. Fellow Chileans Peregrinos open the night. Guitarist Raimundo Santander and New York-based drummer Rodrigo Recabarren cut their first record together in Brooklyn in 2013, and they have used Chilean folk material as a starting point for improvisation ever since. By Friday the Music Room’s stage has to make space for thirteen musicians. Orchestra Mambo International came together in 2022 around Leeds salsa DJ Lubi Jovanovic and trombonist Jonny Enright to play the mambo of Tito Puente, Machito and Eddie Palmieri with a full big-band sound. Trumpets, trombone and baritone sax are stacked over piano, bass, vibraphone and a percussion section of bongos, congas and timbales. Since then they have written their own material, from mambos to cha-cha-chás, much of it gathered on their debut album Apúntalo. Up front, Venezuelan singer Carlos Peña, once a featured vocalist in Oscar D’León‘s orchestra, shares the vocals with Cuban singer Claritzel Miyares. It is the band’s first Liverpool show, and Cuban singer-songwriter George Peguero, returning to La Feria, opens the evening. Saturday night belongs to District, the club on Jordan Street in the Baltic Triangle, where Medellín producer Killabeatmaker sets Afro-Colombian and traditional Colombian rhythms over electronic beats and deep bass. His music keeps returning to the wildlife and landscapes of Colombia and the threats they face. On stage he beatboxes, raps and sings over live beats while Guadalupe Giraldo plays percussion and the gaita, the long, breathy duct flute of Colombia’s Caribbean coast. Opening the night, Mari Merenda plays her first ever UK show. The São Paulo singer/songwriter and producer built her name on videos of the asalato, a West African pair of seed-pod shakers knocked together on a cord. Her songs set forró and coco grooves against pop and R&B with electronic touches, most of them from her 2025 EP Reverbero. In Liverpool she switches between piano and asalato, with Guilherme Monteiro on bass, guitar and vocals, before moving on to Brighton and London. Before District opens its doors on Saturday night, World Museum on William Brown Street hands its galleries over to the festival for a free family day of music, dance, storytelling and workshops. The take-over is part of Cuerpos del Tiempo, a project with the museum’s Global Cultures Collections team to reimagine its Americas Gallery. Artists from eleven countries, from Argentina to Venezuela, perform among the displays. At midday Tamachij Chihuatl, a collective of more than 100 Indigenous Nahua women from Hueyapan in Puebla, Mexico, lead a food workshop. For forty years they have kept their village’s textile tradition alive, weaving wool and colouring it with natural dyes, and their name means “handmade”. La Feria’s free finale takes over The Black-E, the community arts centre on Great George Street, on Sunday. There, Orkney fiddler Catriona Price plays with El Guapo, a Buenos Aires duo on guitar, drums, percussion and vocals who mix Latin American roots with rock and funk. Together they run Routes to Roots, a project that brings musicians from different cultures together to write new music and rework traditional tunes, and which took them to the Edinburgh International Festival in August. Three dance companies share the day. London’s ArtPer UK bring Peruvian folk dances from the coast, the Andes and the Amazon, including the marinera norteña, a courtship dance in which couples circle each other waving handkerchiefs. Colibrí, a Manchester troupe of Mexican dancers led by Guerrero-born choreographer Magaly Flores, perform regional dances in traditional costume, from Veracruz and the Huasteca down to Oaxaca and Chiapas. Inti Tusuy, whose name is Quechua for “sun dance”, bring together dancers with roots in Bolivia, Mexico, Peru and the UK. Latin American food, DJs and dance workshops fill out the afternoon. Once the music stops at The Black-E on Sunday afternoon, the festival’s 2026 theme stays on the walls at Unity Theatre. Belonging, an exhibition by UK-based artists of Latin American heritage, runs there until 6th November, with work drawn from diaspora, ancestry and the places its makers call home.   Full programme and tickets are on the La Feria website The post Event Preview: La Feria 2026 (Liverpool; Wednesday 7th to Sunday 11th October 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Los Angeles duo Patriarchy released an official video for “Lilylicker” on 29 September 2026. The track is the second song on the EP “Appendices,” released 7 August 2026 as a companion to the band’s 2025 album “Manual for Dying.” Appendices by Patriarchy The track opens on a low synth line and a steady kick drum, with Huizenga’s vocals half-whispered through the verses. The arrangement hardens into an industrial-techno beat partway through, with distorted guitars entering on the chorus. Patriarchy describes its own sound as “snuff pop,” a mix of metal, synthpop, punk and dance music. “Appendices” runs five tracks: “Bite Marks,” “Lilylicker,” “Servile,” “Ode (to an Apprehensive Tyrant)” and “Hate Fuck.” Huizenga and English wrote, performed, produced and recorded all five themselves. AJ English mixed “Lilylicker” and Enyang Urbiks mastered it. Witch Club Satan adds backing vocals on “Servile.” The EP is also out as a limited 12-inch clear vinyl edition of 300 copies, shipping around 1 November 2026, alongside digital formats on Bandcamp and streaming services. Patriarchy’s video for ‘Lilylicker’ Patriarchy directed the “Lilylicker” video itself, with cinematography by Hazel Hill McCarthy. Huizenga appears in a white gown holding lilies, then in a pink dress with chains and a metallic corset with gold wings; AJ English, also known as The Drummer, holds a skull and wears white wings. Huizenga’s son also appears in the video. The crew had to relocate the shoot outdoors to the hills above Los Angeles after the original studio balked at the concept and at having a child on set. Huizenga said the move improved the result: “A lot of the things that went ‘wrong’ ultimately added to the beauty of it, like having to shoot outside, where moths kept flying in front of our lenses.” On the project’s name and intent, Huizenga commented: “Patriarchy has never been about perfection, it’s about realizing we are the last remnants of human existence before AI enslaves us all; that’s why the project is called Patriarchy after all.” About Patriarchy Patriarchy formed in Los Angeles as a collaboration between Actually Huizenga and Andrew Means, who met when his band 3TEETH played a show at Das Bunker and offered to work with her in the studio between tour dates. Huizenga had been focused on filmmaking after a prior solo album, “Predator Romantic,” but the sessions with Means led the two to release the songs and build a band around them. Patriarchy released its debut album, “Asking for It,” on 8 November 2019 through Dero Arcade. The band built on that start with “The Unself,” released 26 August 2022, and “Manual for Dying,” out 19 September 2025 and trailed by the singles “Boy on a Leash,” “New Way” and “Die Like Everyone Else.” Patriarchy’s current lineup pairs Huizenga with AJ English, known as The Drummer. The band’s videos, including the earlier live performance clip “No Touch Torture,” are staged and directed largely by Huizenga herself. “Appendices,” the band’s companion EP to “Manual for Dying,” draws on Oscar Wilde, the Marchesa Luisa Casati, the emperor Tiberius and the Manson family as reference points. “Lilylicker” is the second single pulled from that EP, following “Servile,” and its video is Patriarchy’s newest visual release.
items._cn_summary: Patriarchy 是来自洛杉矶的二人组合，自称"snuff pop"，将金属、合成器流行、朋克与舞曲融为一体。EP《Appendices》共五首曲目，延续其2025年专辑《Manual for Dying》的暗黑基调。《Lilylicker》以低频合成器线条与稳定底鼓开场，人声半呢喃于verse段落，中段过渡为工业techno节拍，副歌加入失真吉他。《Appendices》以限量300张透明黑胶与数字形式发行，制作由二人独立完成。MV由乐队自导，Huizenga身着白裙手持百合，后换粉色裙装与金属胸甲，AJ English持骷髅头戴白色翅膀，场景从室内转至洛杉矶山间外景，借飞蛾入镜增添画面质感。乐队以"人类在AI奴役前的最后残余"为创作宣言，作品带有明显的反乌托邦美学与仪式感。整体而言，这张EP在工业与暗潮交叉地带探索，融合电子节拍与摇滚吉他，呈现出较为独特的视觉与声音结合。

items.excerpt: ここ15年のヒップホップ／R&Bの裏方として欠かせぬ存在となった奇才の初リーダー作。オルタナティヴな音楽を好んだ自身の趣味と世間のステレオタイプな黒人像との間で板挟みになった少年時代を回顧しながら内省を深めていく内容で、ロックやジャズ、アフリカ音楽などの要素も交え、ポリリズムを活かした型破りなビートで自由な音楽観を描いていく。ケンドリック・ラマー、チャイルディッシュ・ガンビーノ、ヴィンス・ステイプルズ、ジェシー・ボイキンズ3世、モーゼス・サムニー、フーシェ、レイヴン・レネーなど、縁のあるゲストたちの名前からも推し量れるオルタナ感全開の怪作だ。

It features the German band's full score, as well as new reworks of the track 'Steiner's Ecstasy' by james K, ML Buch and Lorenzo Senni. Herzog's film told the story of Walter Steiner, a Swiss ski jumper who was chasing a world record in ski flying while also working full-time as a carpenter and indulging in his hobby of... The post Popol Vuh Score for 1974 Werner Herzog Film to Get First Official Release appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Popol Vuh 为赫尔佐格1974年纪录片《木雕师施泰纳的伟大迷狂》所写的配乐，此前只能以粉丝翻录的形式被聆听，如今迎来首度黑胶正式发行。专辑包含德国乐队完整的电影配乐作品，同时收录了三位当代音乐人对主题曲目《施泰纳的迷狂》的重新演绎：James K、ML Buch 与 Lorenzo Senni 各自带来不同方向的电子化改写。这张配乐是 Popol Vuh 将迷幻空间感与新世纪氛围注入电影声音设计的早期范例，与赫尔佐格镜头中瑞士跳台滑雪运动员 Walter Steiner 的追逐纪录形成听觉层面的呼应。作为 Krautrock 谱系中偏向氛围与冥想气质的代表作品，它对后世 ambient 与电子音乐场景产生了持续影响，本次官方发行为乐迷提供了完整的聆听入口。

Dara Kiely comes in screaming on ‘The Angelus’, all scalded shriek, hollering about Bananas in Pyjamas and Gary Lineker as crisp maniac. The track pitches somewhere between Lightning Bolt and a ten-thousand-mile thundercloud, Adam Faulkner’s rolls hurtling underneath like Swans at triple speed. items._cn_summary: Gilla Band以新专辑《Pugnello》呈现了其迄今最具压迫感的作品。开篇曲《The Angelus》中主唱Dara Kiely以灼烧般的嘶吼开场，将爱尔兰国家电视台晚祷钟声的概念重塑为街头传教士的狂乱布道。编曲上，Adam Faulkner的鼓击以接近Lightning Bolt的速度推进，低频厚重如雷云，Swans式的密集压迫感贯穿全作。歌词文本将Bananas in Pyjamas与Gary Lineker等流行文化符号并置，制造出荒诞而尖锐的间离效果。乐队延续自《France 98》以来的创作脉络，在噪音摇滚与后朋克框架内注入更多实验性张力。整体制作注重原始冲击力与节奏驱动的身体性反应，刻意削弱旋律的舒适度以换取聆听过程中的紧张感。

items.body: Review by ChuChu — One of my favourite albums of all time and, in my opinion everyone who likes the later more proggy Floyd stuff should give it a listen. The album mostly written by Syd Barrett, features tons of experimental and psychedelic stuff that no other album by Pink Floyd and any other band replicates. Astronomy Domine is a great opener track with a great instrumental part in the middle, Flaming and Matilda Mother evoke in me the feeling of childhood, Interstellar Overdrive and Lucifer Sam are really catchy psychedelic tracks and The Gnome feels like reading "Lord Of The Rings" and "Hobbit" all over again.I love this album, it has a great selection of tracks and a really fun vibe to it, would recommend this album to someone who wants to get into Pink Floyd but only knows "The Dark Side Of The Moon" and "Wish You Were Here"

items._cn_summary: 这是Pink Floyd首张专辑，由Syd Barrett主导创作，整体充满迷幻与实验色彩。专辑开篇曲《Astronomy Domine》以中段器乐即兴段落展现出鲜明的太空感与自由探索气质；《Flaming》与《Matilda Mother》营造出童真与梦境交织的氛围；《Interstellar Overdrive》与《Lucifer Sam》则以抓耳的迷幻旋律和吉他音色见长；《The Gnome》的叙事风格带有托尔金式的奇幻文学色彩。整张专辑在1967年英式摇滚语境下极具前瞻性，大量音效处理与即兴段落为后来的前卫摇滚发展埋下伏笔，是了解Pink Floyd早期创作脉络的重要入口。

items.body: “Curandera” opens Bestiaria with a healer giving instructions. “Niña / Escucha cómo tu cuerpo te habla,” sings Ana Karen G. Barajas of Karen y Los Remedios: girl, listen to how your body talks to you. The song comes from Karen’s own illness and from the women in her family who saw her through it with advice, recipes and limpias, the cleansing rituals Mexican grandmothers pass down. The curandera in the lyric hands the work back to the girl, telling her to listen to her body and to how her soul breathes, and warns her that “Cuando callas te guardas / Lo malo / Y lo bueno”: stay silent and you keep the bad in with the good. Karen, guitarist Guillermo Berbeyer and Mexico City producer Jiony set it as a dark cumbia over a low bass and a steady beat. Trombone and cowbell sit around her voice, an organ hangs at the back of the mix, and in the instrumental breaks synth and guitar lines take over. She lives in Hong Kong now, a long way from the Mexico City she was born in and the Guanajuato she grew up in. Bestiaria, the follow-up to 2023’s Silencio, builds its twelve songs around twelve figures, among them the agave goddess Mayahuel and the Fates of “Las Moiras”. “Curandera” is the fourth single from it. Listen to “Curandera” HERE and pre-order Bestiaria, out on 9 October via ZZK Records, following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Karen y los Remedios – Curandera appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: Karen y los Remedios 的单曲《Curandera》以低沉贝斯与稳定节拍构建暗黑昆比亚氛围，长号、牛铃与风琴点缀人声，器乐间奏由合成器与吉他交替主导。主唱 Ana Karen G. Barajas 取材于自身患病经历与家族女性的疗愈传统，将墨西哥祖母辈流传的 limpias 净化仪式融入歌词，传递倾听身体与灵魂呼吸的信息。整张专辑《Bestiaria》以十二首歌对应十二个女性意象，包括龙舌兰女神 Mayahuel 与命运之神 Las Moiras。艺术家现居香港，远离墨西哥城与瓜纳华托的故乡，ZZK Records 厂牌发行。

items.body: My sins are all forgiven. I might be desperate, but I won’t let you forget. I know you will give in to me. I am dead set. I am dead set. She 1 • Him 2 have built their latest single Obsessed around one of pop music’s most reliable bad ideas: somebody confusing romantic destiny with a complete inability to take no for an answer. The Cleveland duo of Evan Nave and Cassie Bishop bring years of Lestat and Shy Moon behind them, though Obsessed feels leaner and brighter than that résumé might suggest. The synths skip forward in sharp little patterns, Bishop keeps her vocal airy and cool, and underneath it all sits an electroclash streak that brings to mind the clipped attitude and wiry pop economy of Elastica fed through a rack of 80s electronics. There is plenty of Human League, Yazoo, Soft Cell, and Ladytron in the bloodstream, but the guitars give the track an extra shove. Producer Michael Seifert threads in parts with a distinctly Fixx-like character, adding just enough bite to keep the arrangement from becoming too polished for its own good. “This song has been amazing to put together,” says Nave. “An 80s vibe with a very modern spin. And our producer, Michael Seifert, dropped some very Fixx-like guitars on it. Love the dark lyrical tone versus the upbeat music dichotomy.” That contrast is where Obsessed starts getting funny in a slightly alarming way. The music suggests somebody having a marvelous time under bright club lights; the lyrics suggest that somebody has already memorized your commute. Bishop drew inspiration from the horror film Obsession and its character Nikki, played by Inde Navarrette. “I wrote the lyrics to this song based off the movie Obsession, which I loved and thought was a unique and fun idea for a horror movie,” says Bishop. “I wanted to capture some of the elements and mood of the film in this piece.” She certainly found the right emotional neighborhood. The character at the center of the song barrels through pleading, certainty, possession, and total romantic entitlement while treating every objection as a temporary inconvenience. Love becomes less a mutual arrangement than a hostile takeover conducted in excellent makeup. Bishop wisely keeps her delivery light. She never overplays the menace, and that restraint makes the character more convincing. The voice remains smooth, composed, almost sweet, even as the lyrics tighten their grip. It gives Obsessed the unnerving quality of someone smiling pleasantly while explaining why the two of you are obviously meant to spend eternity together. The electroclash edge helps, too. Those angular guitars and bright electronics give the song a brisk, fashionable nastiness, somewhere between synthpop precision and the kind of deadpan cool Elastica once made look effortless. Obsessed is catchy enough to dance to and unhinged enough to make you reconsider sharing your location. Romance, apparently, remains a dangerous hobby. The charming video channels that same bubbly sycophancy inside the studio, where eager autograph and selfie seekers chase the performers around, hoping for — and eventually fighting over — a moment with their idols. There is something wonderfully silly about the escalation, and visually it brings to mind Toni Basil’s Mickey, with its bright, performative enthusiasm and choreographed fan frenzy. The joke fits the song neatly: admiration is only one bad decision away from fixation. Watch the video for Obsessed below: Listen to Obsessed below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: She 1 • Him 2 的单曲《Obsessed》以明亮的合成器节拍和电吉他织体构建出冷调舞曲骨架，融汇了 Human League、Yazoo、Soft Cell、Ladytron 等八十年代合成器流行血脉，同时带有 Elastica 式的尖锐朋克态度与 The Fixx 式的吉他锋芒。歌词与音乐之间形成刻意反差——欢快轻盈的旋律包裹着偏执与占有欲的主题，主唱以冷静克制的声线传递出令人不安的亲密暴力，灵感来源于恐怖电影《Obsession》中的角色 Nikki。制作人 Michael Seifert 在编排上保持了适度粗糙感，避免过度抛光。整体呈现出一首具备合成器流行精确度与暗潮式病态美学的作品，适合喜欢复古电子音色与叙事张力并存的听众。
